steps.action: Revoke the elevated session immediately. Disable the admin account used if it is not a known service account.
Isolate the source host — the escalation may indicate a compromised endpoint running local exploits.
Determine how escalation occurred: sudo misconfig, SUID binary, token impersonation, or stolen credentials.
Audit what the admin account did after escalation — check command history, file access, and outbound connections.
Patch or reconfigure the escalation vector. Rotate all credentials on the affected host.
Implement least-privilege. Enable privileged-access workstation (PAW) and session recording for admin accounts.
Document escalation path, affected accounts, and remediation steps taken.
